title: Nocturnal animals
examples: How do bats fly at night?
Do all animals that are awake at night live in the dark?

explain.say: Today we learn about animals that are active at night. These animals are called nocturnal creatures. They sleep when the sun is shining brightly.
Let us look at the owl. Owls have very big eyes that help them see in the dark. They can hunt for food when it is dark outside.
Next, we learn about bats. Bats use their good hearing to find their way around. They make sounds that bounce off things.
Foxes are also often seen at night. They have excellent senses to help them find food. They are clever animals that move quietly.
So, owls use big eyes, and bats use good hearing. Foxes use their senses to survive the night. These are amazing adaptations for life after sunset.
A common mistake is thinking all animals that are out at night are nocturnal. Some animals are just active at night for other reasons. Nocturnal means their main activity time is at night.

faq.q: Why do owls have such big eyes?
faq.a: Owls have large eyes because they need to collect as much light as possible. This helps them see clearly when it is very dark outside.
asks: How do owls see in the dark?
Are owl eyes bigger than human eyes?

faq.q: What is echo location for bats?
faq.a: Echo location is when bats make sounds and listen to the returning echoes. This helps them map out their surroundings in the dark.
asks: How do bats navigate without light?
Do bats use sound like sonar?

faq.q: Do all animals that are awake at night are mammals?
faq.a: No, not all nocturnal animals are mammals. Some nocturnal animals, like certain birds, are not mammals at all.

faq.q: Are foxes always active at night?
faq.a: Foxes are often seen hunting at dawn or dusk, which is sometimes called crepuscular. They are very adaptable hunters.
asks: Do foxes only come out at night?

faq.q: What is the main difference between a bat and an owl?
faq.a: The main difference is how they find food. Owls rely mostly on their excellent eyesight, while bats use sound echoes.
asks: Do bats see better than owls?
What sense do they use most?

facts: Bats use sound waves for navigation.
Foxes are known for being clever hunters.
Nocturnal means active at night time.

quiz.say: Which animal relies heavily on its big eyes for night hunting?
quiz.why: The owl is specifically known for its powerful eyesight to hunt in low light.

wrong.0: Bats primarily use sound echoes, not just sight.
wrong.1: Foxes use a mix of senses, but the owl's vision is the key feature here.
wrong.2: Each animal has a different main sense for the night.

quiz.say: What sense do bats use to map their environment?
quiz.why: Bats create and listen to echoes, which is a form of using sound.

wrong.0: They do not rely on touch to navigate large areas at night.
wrong.2: While they can see, sound is their primary tool for mapping.
wrong.3: Smell is important, but sound is their unique navigation method.

quiz.say: If an animal is only active after the sun sets, what is it called?
quiz.why: Nocturnal means the animal is most active during the night hours.

wrong.0: This is not the correct scientific term for night activity.
wrong.2: Diurnal means the animal is active during the daytime.
wrong.3: Crepuscular means active at dawn or dusk, not all night.
